task.title: Activate selected tool components atomically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/627 by composing preparation, compilation, inert adapter construction, and caller-owned registry registration.
acceptance_criteria: Expose one root-to-registry operation without invoking guest code.
Commit deterministic exact-ID pure tools only after the entire selected batch succeeds.
Leave the registry unchanged on preparation, compilation, construction, or duplicate-ID failure.
Make empty selection a filesystem-free successful no-op.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for atomic root-to-registry activation.
attempts.diagnostic: No activation operation or staged activation error existed, and the kernel registry had no atomic batch registration primitive.
attempts.patch: Added activation tests for success, rollback, exact metadata, unsupported kinds, duplicates, and inert guest behavior plus registry batch tests.

attempts.diagnostic: Completing preparation, compilation, and adapter construction before a preflighted homogeneous registry batch preserves existing registry state on every failure.
attempts.patch: Added activate_tool_selection, ToolActivationError, ToolRegistry::register_all, docs, and milestone evidence.

attempts.summary: Fixed empty activation after independent review.
attempts.diagnostic: The first implementation called preparation for an empty selection and therefore touched a root that the contract required it to ignore.
attempts.patch: Added a RED regression that removes the root before empty activation, then returned early before filesystem access.

outcome.summary: Selected tool components now activate into caller-owned registries atomically, remain inert until authorized invocation, and treat empty intent as a filesystem-free no-op.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-extensions --test activation
GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30212234807 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/628

lessons: Atomic registration requires preflighting both existing collisions and duplicates inside the incoming batch.
Staged typed errors preserve which trust boundary failed without exposing partial activation.
An empty operation should avoid even prerequisite filesystem access when the contract promises a no-op.
Independent review is most valuable when it turns a subtle contract mismatch into a focused regression test.
